CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain at the end of right middle finger

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
41-year-old female with right middle finger pain of 4-5 days duration. Injury occurred during a motor vehicle accident while patient was stopped at a four-way stop. Patient was rear-ended by another vehicle; patient suspects driver was texting. Patient became angry and attempted to flip off the other driver, striking the ceiling of the car. Minimal vehicle damage with crumpling of trunk. X-ray reveals distal phalanx fracture of right middle finger. Physical examination shows tenderness over distal phalanx.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No other injuries from motor vehicle accident reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident 4-5 days ago.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Tenderness over distal phalanx of right middle finger. No tenderness in lower aspects of finger. Otherwise normal examination.

RESULTS
X-ray of right middle finger: Distal phalanx fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of right middle finger. Tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain (8 tablets dispensed). Confirmed Tramadol is safe with concurrent Digoxin use. Finger splint applied. Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks.
